author: A N M Bazlur Rahman
html: “The virtual thread scheduler is a work-stealing ForkJoinPool, which is distinct from the common pool.” That’s what it is mentioned in the JEP: 425, though.

author: Miro Wengner
html:
Good point! dev state seems to consider common thread pool for executing the real work as VirtualThreads are not bind to real worker Thread (see. Image 1) I’m adding a following current implementation code private static final Executor ASYNC_POOL = USE_COMMON_POOL ? ForkJoinPool.commonPool() : new ThreadPerTaskExecutor();
where USE_COMMON_POOL=TRUE. FALSE case could be “challenging” as it’d start a new not daemon Threads. Let’s wait till the upcoming JDK19 release as VirtualThreads are scheduled there as a 1st Preview.
